note: Risk-off week, and the character changed on Friday. S&P 500 -1.01% to 7,457.69, Nasdaq -1.4% to 25,520.24, Dow -0.77% to 52,146.42 — the S&P closed below its 200-day moving average (7,472.59) for the first time since Apr 8. The driver is a genuine loss of faith in the AI-chip trade rather than a macro shock: SOXX fell 4.5% on Jul 16 and TSMC's blowout print (profit +77% y/y, revenue +36%) could not hold the ADR up. JPMorgan flagged the widening split between chipmakers and the hyperscalers funding them as 'somewhat unsustainable'. Meanwhile the Gulf war escalated — Kuwait said Iran struck a power and desalination plant, US Central Command completed a sixth consecutive night of strikes, and Hormuz crossings fell about 52% week-on-week. Brent jumped 4.6% to $88.10, up more than 14% on the week, and XLE (+1.42%) was the leading sector while refining margins hit records. Rates were calm: 10Y 4.55%, 2Y 4.18%, curve positively sloped at +0.37, Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75% into Jul 28-29. VIX 18.03, up ~20% on the week but still below 20 — complacency is fading, not gone.
